lead.headline: The US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, calling them defensive strikes, on the eve of the midterm elections
lead.short: Several explosions hit Iran's Qeshm Island late on Monday, and US officials told The Wall Street Journal and AP that the US military had carried out what they called defensive strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. The targets were Iranian forces using surface-to-air missiles against US assets, one official said. Blasts were also heard in the port of Bandar Lengeh.

why.text: Any return to fighting in Hormuz threatens the talks that pushed oil down this week, and Indian ships and seafarers are already being hit there.

more: Witnesses told Iran's IRNA news agency they saw two planes over the island, which lies off Iran's southern coast. Fox News and Axios said the strikes answered the Revolutionary Guards firing at a US aircraft on Monday, and a US official told Fox it was not "the start of expanded strikes". One official told the Journal that Washington had kept the campaign quiet to avoid signalling a return to major combat.

Earlier on Monday the Guards said they had captured two US reconnaissance drones south of Qeshm using electronic warfare and destroyed an MQ-9 drone east of the strait. There was no immediate comment from Tehran or Washington. Brent crude rose 1.6% to about $106.50 on Tuesday, after falling 3.5% on Monday on hopes for the Qatar-mediated talks.

facts.targets: Qeshm Island; blasts also at Bandar Lengeh

update.new: The US has struck Qeshm Island.
update.front: The first US strikes on Iranian soil since the talks began put the Hormuz deal at risk.

seconds.headline: An Indian seafarer is killed when an aerial object hits the vessel Al Jusufi off Oman, and 13 crew are rescued
seconds.short: Gandhar Nahim Ajij, a seafarer from Gujarat, was killed when the Indian vessel MSV Al Jusufi was struck by an "unidentified aerial object" near Limah, off Oman, on Monday, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal said. The other 13 Indians aboard were rescued by the Omani coast guard. The foreign ministry called for an immediate de-escalation in West Asia.

why.text: Indian crews keep paying for the war at sea, and this attack came hours before the US struck Iran in the same waters.

more: "The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest," the Ministry of External Affairs said. It urged the conclusion of the negotiations for a diplomatic solution.

The Indian embassy in Oman is working with Omani authorities to bring home the 13 survivors and Ajij's body. Last week limpet mines hit the tanker MT Louise 1, with 27 Indian crew aboard, in the Strait of Hormuz; all of them survived. Officials have not said who launched the object that hit the Al Jusufi.

update.new: An Indian seafarer has been killed off Oman.
update.front: The war at sea has now killed an Indian sailor on an Indian vessel.

seconds.headline: Americans vote today for control of Congress, with prices and the Iran war weighing on Trump's Republicans
seconds.short: Americans vote in the midterm elections on Tuesday, deciding control of Congress for Donald Trump's last two years. Voters say the cost of living is their main worry, with food and fuel prices up partly because of his tariffs and the war with Iran. The Supreme Court on Monday refused to let California set aside 20,000 ballots.

why.text: A Democratic Congress would check Trump on tariffs and the war, both of which shape India's trade and its fuel bill.

more: Trump, facing record low approval ratings, has held dozens of rallies, including in Iowa and Kansas, normally safe Republican ground. "When they start spending hard American dollars on political advertising in a state that they should be winning, that's how you know that they think they're in trouble," said Carrie Dann of the Cook Political Report. In his final speech he spent much of an hour on repairs to the Reflecting Pool in Washington.

The Trump administration had asked the Supreme Court to have California set aside the mail ballots of 20,000 people it called likely non-citizens; state officials said the list was full of errors. Results begin after polls close, from about 05:30 IST on Wednesday.

facts.California ballots: 20,000; Supreme Court refused to set them aside

update.new: Polling day; the Supreme Court rejects the California ballot push.
update.front: The vote that decides how much of a free hand Trump keeps is happening today.

seconds.headline: Anthropic's revenue jumps to $17bn in the third quarter ahead of its IPO, as its filing warns it is close to AI that improves itself
seconds.short: Anthropic said on Monday that its revenue reached $17bn in the third quarter, up from $1.4bn a year earlier, in an amended filing for a stock market listing expected as early as next week. Its net loss was $23.3bn, mostly non-cash charges, and it has committed to spend about $895bn, mostly on computing power.

why.text: It is the biggest test yet of whether investors will pay for the AI boom, and the first chance for ordinary investors to buy a big AI lab directly.

more: The company slipped back to an operating loss of $567m in the quarter as it paid more for short-term computing capacity. Its filing of about 400 pages gives more than 90 pages to risks. Investors are pushing for a valuation closer to $1.5 trillion, as nerves about AI spending hit big tech shares last week.

New risk language in the filing says Anthropic already uses AI in its research and development and is approaching what has been called "recursive self-improvement", TechCrunch reports. "Using AI to help build more capable AI could also pose a considerable safety risk, particularly if it sharply accelerates the pace of progress," the filing says, adding that its Responsible Scaling Policy covers how it plans to monitor the risks.

update.new: The amended filing: $17bn quarterly revenue and an RSI warning.
update.front: The figures and the risk warning come days before the biggest AI listing yet.

seconds.headline: Russian bombs kill at least 29 people at a school used to hand out aid in Zaporizhzhia, days after a truce ended
seconds.short: At least 29 people were killed when at least nine 3,000kg Russian aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region on Monday, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said. The first struck a school used for aid distribution and a second hit where people sheltered, said Volodymyr Zelensky, who called it "utterly horrific". Another 48 people are missing.

why.text: It ends the brief hope from last week's local truce, and with it the chance of wider talks soon.

more: Ten people were injured. Ukraine's emergency service said two rescuers and four police officers were among the dead. Rescue teams have had to stop several times because of Russian drones overhead, Semikin said, and a day of mourning has been declared across the region on Tuesday.

"The Russians could not have been unaware that the local residents who remained in Komyshuvakha received humanitarian aid there every week," Zelensky said. He said that after the joint evacuation of civilians from occupied Oleshky during the ceasefire there had been "a moment when the next steps could show that peace is possible", but that Russia was "counting on further killings".

update.new: Russia's deadliest strike since the truce ended.
update.front: The deadliest attack in weeks came as soon as the local truce ended.

stories.headline: The Bombay High Court orders the BMC to restore Dia Mirza's firecracker-free Diwali video, pulled after BJP objections
stories.short: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday expressed its "deep pain and displeasure" over the row about actor Dia Mirza's video for the BMC's eco-friendly Deepavali campaign, and ordered the civic body to re-upload it. The BMC had removed the clip on Monday after Mumbai BJP chief Ameet Satam objected and Mayor Ritu Tawde called her "anti-Hindu".

why.text: A court has stepped in to stop a pollution campaign being turned into a religious fight, days before Diwali.

more: Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale took up the matter on their own and said they were anguished by the "petty mindset" of certain people, especially elected representatives. "India is a secular country," the bench said, calling it "most unfortunate" that a video about air and noise pollution had been given such a colour.

The BMC had asked citizens to avoid firecrackers after an earlier High Court direction on Mumbai's air. Only Mirza's clip was taken down; videos by Madhuri Dixit, Nishigandha Wad and the cricketer Ajinkya Rahane stayed up. The court said the commissioner was right in choosing the celebrities and no one could question why a particular one was picked.

facts.bench: Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale

stories.headline: Indian Navy commandos airdropped from a C-17 retake a hijacked fishing vessel off Somalia and free all 20 crew
stories.short: The Indian Navy has rescued the fishing vessel Azini from armed pirates off northeastern Somalia in an operation lasting more than 48 hours, freeing all 20 crew without casualties. The boat, hijacked last month, was suspected of serving as a 'mother ship' for attacks on merchant ships. The crew are Iranian, according to reports of the navy's statement.

why.text: It shows the navy's reach in the Arabian Sea at a time when Indian ships in the region are being attacked.

more: A warship and a maritime reconnaissance aircraft tracked the Azini, and the navy used what it called "calibrated non-kinetic measures" to stop it escaping. Marine commandos were then airdropped by an Indian Air Force C-17, boarded the vessel and "neutralised the pirate threat", the navy said.

The rescue took more than 48 hours from start to finish. The navy said the operation reinforced India's role as a 'First Responder' and 'Preferred Security Partner' in the Indian Ocean. Piracy has returned off Somalia as the West Asia war stretches naval forces in the region, and the UN has just ended its political mission in Somalia after three decades.

briefs.text: Demand fell 29% to 162.5 tonnes in the September quarter as jewellery buying dropped 20% and investment 40%, with high prices and the weakest monsoon in over a decade hurting rural buyers. Diwali and weddings should lift the December quarter.

stories.headline: Apple sets an all-time revenue record in India and iPhone sales rise 17%, but it cannot say when Duo shortages will end
stories.short: Apple's iPhone revenue rose 17% to $57.6bn in the September quarter, and India set an all-time revenue record, chief executive John Ternus said on Monday. He told Reuters Apple is "not able to predict when supply and demand will be in balance" for the $1,999 iPhone Duo, and warned that memory costs will rise further this quarter.

why.text: India is now one of Apple's fastest-growing markets, and rising memory costs are already pushing up phone prices there.

more: "We grew in the vast majority of markets we tracked," Ternus said, with September-quarter records in the Americas, Europe, Greater China and the rest of Asia-Pacific. India also had a record number of people upgrading their iPhones, and all-time records for Mac and services, Counterpoint's Tarun Pathak noted.

Preorders for the Duo, Apple's first foldable, sold out, with some deliveries now due in 2027. Ternus said "a very small percentage" were returned with cracked screens and are being replaced. "What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented," he said; Apple has raised prices across its range, and expects a lower margin in the holiday quarter.

facts.Duo: no date for supply to meet demand

update.new: Results: record India revenue; Duo shortages with no end date.

briefs.headline: Google says a Chinese partner built a backdoor into 1.3 million Android TV boxes and ran them as a botnet
briefs.text: Shenzhen-based Videostrong sold access to criminals for ad fraud and proxy networks, Google said, and has been banned from making certified Android devices. Taking down affiliated servers cuts off at least 10 million more infected devices.

briefs.headline: NASA's Swift observatory is expected to fall back to Earth on Wednesday at about 14:00 IST, give or take 11 hours
briefs.text: Re-entry is predicted for about 14:00 IST, with 11 hours either way. Most of the 1,450 kg spacecraft should burn up, but any surviving pieces could land between 20.6 degrees south and north, NASA says. It puts the risk of anyone being hurt at one in 2,100.

facts.re-entry: Wed 4 Nov, about 08:30 GMT, plus or minus 11 hours

briefs.text: Rice set up Kai Havertz's 16th-minute goal. Arsenal have now won at four grounds where they failed to win last season, and Peter Schmeichel tipped them for the title.

update.new: Rice's verdict; first league win at Anfield since 2012.

briefs.headline: Gotham FC win the NWSL Shield on the league's biggest Decision Day, with all 16 teams playing at once
briefs.text: The league had simulated the final day 50,000 times and found 6,561 possible combinations of results. ESPN showed all eight games for the first time, with more than 60 cameras.

briefs.headline: Australia's 'Big Show' Maxwell retires from international cricket after 286 matches and three world titles
briefs.text: The 38-year-old won three world titles, scored 7,226 runs and took 136 wickets, and shares the T20I record of five hundreds with Rohit Sharma. His unbeaten 201 against Afghanistan at the Wankhede in the 2023 World Cup is his best-remembered innings.

briefs.headline: The first India-Sri Lanka ODI on 13 December is likely to be moved out of Delhi over pollution
briefs.text: The DDCA has asked the BCCI to shift the match, citing air quality and renovation at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, Cricbuzz reports. In 2017 some Sri Lankan players were sick on the field during a Delhi Test.
